events.name: Critical Thinking Club
events.description:
New Yorkers argue a lot. Disagreement has the power to bring us closer together, but most of us never learned how. Somewhere along the way, speed replaced clarity, and certainty replaced curiosity. The result: we're more polarized, and less understanding.

​Critical Thinking Club aims to reverse that trend by providing space for busy New Yorkers who want to think more clearly and communicate more thoughtfully. The goal isn’t to "win" an argument, it’s to improve how we listen, disagree, and express our opinions without distancing each other.

​Our next theme is, "When you move away, do you owe home anything, or only yourself?"

​We’ll use this topic to practice critical thinking skills like…

​Articulating views you disagree with

​Separating personal experience from broader evidence

​Noticing hidden assumptions, in yourself and others

​Revising your position without compromising your values or credibility

​What to expect

​2 comedians debate and a philosophy professor moderates

​Small-group conversations with guided prompts

​A psychologically safe environment for disagreement

​The evening begins with a moderated discussion between 2 comedians who take opposite sides. A professor of philosophy moderates and steps in when reasoning breaks down, or a common fallacy appears. The moderator pauses to explain, and suggests how reasoning could be improved. Mistakes are expected and useful. The goal is for all of us to share the learnings. Then, everyone practices in small groups.

​Agenda

​6:30 - 7 PM - Arrive, grab a refreshment, chat, find a seat

​7 - 7:05 PM - Summarize what to expect, introduce the moderator and speakers

​7:05 - 7:35 PM - Opening statements, Q&A, and closing statements

​7:35 - 8:05 - Small group discussions (4-6 people) to practice sound critical thinking skills with the help of guided prompts

​8:05 - 8:10 - Wrap-up, participants can share key takeaways from their group discussions

​8:10 - 8:45ish - Socialize with the speakers and participants

​9 - after party Puffy's Tavern

​Speakers

​We’re excited to have Greg Nirshberg moderating our next discussion. Greg is the Professor of Philosophy at Iona University, an advisor for the university’s interdisciplinary neuroscience program, and he received his Ph.D. in philosophy at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2023, https://www.iona.edu/faculty/nirshberg-gregory

​Our next speakers will be announced soon!

​If you want to understand others better, and be better understood, join us!

events.name: Drinking Chocolate With Prophecy Chocolate
events.description:
It is 2 pm on a Tuesday at Fabrik and you could use a pick me up while you get your work done. Luckily for all of us, Mateo of Prophecy chocolate will be coming down from Vermont to take care of you. He will make you a cup of chocolate and show you how to make a good one too. The chocolate drinking will only be about 30 minutes, but feel free to hang around, ask questions and chat. This is your chance to get a little nurturing and some great chocolate in the middle of the workday. Tuesday just got so much better.

AND....that is not all. We have a special guest straight from Oaxaca. His sister-in-law owns Sobre Masa in Brooklyn, a well respected restaurant featuring Oaxacan cuisine.

Gregorio is a master weaver and is a member of the only family in the region that is still fermenting a cousin of cacao called Theobroma Bicolor. It’s RARE and helps to create the beloved froth on some chocolate drinks. This is an extremely rare opportunity. Gregorio is also a master weaver who makes natural dyes. If you have ever wanted to visit Oaxaca, this is the closest you will get to it on a workday.

This is a free event for FABRIK MEMBERS.

Who are we?

Mateo is the founder of Prophecy Chocolate in Vermont. Mateo has spent years living in Peru, Colombia, and Mexico, learning directly from campesinos how cacao is grown, harvested, and transformed. In 2014, while living in the “Eyebrow of the Jungle” in Peru, he learned to make drinking chocolate using traditional methods, an experience that shaped his lifelong love for cacao.

He later imported heirloom cacao from the Cusco jungle and apprenticed in European‑style chocolate making. In 2019 he founded Prophecy Chocolate, creating craft chocolate from direct‑trade cacao. In 2025 and 2026, Prophecy Chocolate earned 13 medals in the International Chocolate Awards.

Mateo teaches about cacao at expos and universities, and when he isn’t making chocolate, he’s often on farms or in the forest, learning from growers and enjoying the plants that inspire his work

Nettie is the founder of The Chocolate Connection.

I create guided chocolate experiences that combine storytelling, history, sensory exploration, and first-hand stories gathered through years of traveling to cacao farms, meeting growers and chocolate makers, and exploring chocolate traditions around the world.

Chocolate is simply the starting point.

Through shared tasting, conversation, and immersive storytelling, guests gain a deeper appreciation for the people, cultures, and craftsmanship behind chocolate while creating meaningful connections with one another.

Every experience is designed to leave people feeling more present, more connected, and inspired to keep exploring long after the experience ends.

events.name: The Kalshi Crisis: Bets Over Baghdad
events.description:
Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN and CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there.

​So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch?

​For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders.

​For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, and worse actors. Polymarket and Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had.

​One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market.

​Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology and the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, and contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, and Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households and classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies.

​Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, and has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal and compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF and a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, and roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant.

​Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have.

​Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, and Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair and New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days and elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race and calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided.

​Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Sex, Crime, Gender: Hollywood and the Rise of Censorship
events.description:
A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.

Here's what you need to know!
We will begin with a short introduction and a film screening of the 1933 film Design for Living. After the screening, Matt Johnson will walk us through how the film is an insight into censorship.

Most people think of film history as a straight line — movies started out conservative and gradually pushed toward the sex and violence of today's blockbusters. That's not what happened.

Early Hollywood talkies were surprisingly bold. Frank depictions of sexuality, violence, and gender norms played out on screen at a moment of real cultural upheaval in America. It was freewheeling, daring, and genuinely revolutionary — until religious authorities, alarmed by what they called "filth" in America's mass media, began pushing back. Hard. The result was a self-imposed Hollywood Code that would reshape what American audiences were allowed to see for decades.

Sound familiar? America is currently in the middle of a strikingly similar cultural battle — book bans, library defunding, and political pressure on broadcasters are reshaping what people can access right now. Film historian Matt Johnson traces the arc from Pre-Code Hollywood to the rise of censorship — and makes the case that attempts to silence artistic output almost always produce something more subversive and more clever in return.
Matt Johnson teaches film theory and history at Franklin and Marshall College, where he is also a Fellow coordinating work in refugee resettlement and the question of welcome. He brings the same intellectual rigor and genuine curiosity to the history of Hollywood that he does to the most pressing questions of our time.

We'll explore:
* The surprisingly bold and daring films that existed before Hollywood self-censorship — and why they matter
* How religious, political, and cultural forces converged to impose the Hollywood Code
* Ernst Lubitsch and the "Lubitsch Touch" — how European filmmaking influenced and challenged Hollywood norms
* Why America has been here before — and what the history of censorship tells us about the cultural battles happening right now
* How artists have historically defeated censorship — and what that looks like today

Session 2: What we will cover: 

Build a month of social content, scheduled and running, in one evening.

What’s covered

Build a repeatable social media engine from end to end, covering strategy and brand voice, content creation and repurposing, visuals, scheduling, publishing, audience engagement, and performance measurement.

The goal is not simply to generate a pile of posts. You’ll create a system that helps you consistently publish, engage, and learn what is actually growing your audience.

What you’ll do

Set the strategy

Define your positioning, your audience, and the two or three channels that are genuinely worth your time.
Capture your brand voice as a reusable Claude skill so your content does not sound generic.

Create the content

Generate a month of social posts.
Repurpose one central idea into multiple formats across different platforms.
Draft accompanying visuals and sharpen every hook, caption, and call to action.

Schedule and publish

Load and schedule the entire month of content across your platforms using Metricool.

Engage and measure

Manage direct messages and comments from one unified inbox.
Turn on an analytics loop, connect the results to Claude, and identify which content deserves more investment.

Recommended stack: Claude for voice and copy, AirOps for producing content at volume, Metricool for scheduling, engagement, and analytics, and Canva for visuals.

Other tools considered: Claude alone for a simpler content workflow, Buffer for straightforward and affordable scheduling, Later for visual and Instagram-first brands, and Hootsuite for larger enterprise teams.

You’ll leave with: A full month of scheduled content and a repeatable marketing engine you can operate in roughly one hour per week.

events.name: How to Turn Trains Into Music
events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
 💭 Topic: "How to Turn Trains Into Music" 🎤 Lecturer: Joshua Wolk 📆 Date: Friday, September 4th  ⏰ Doors Open: 6:30 PM 📍 Location: Tribeca, Manhattan
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
🤝 A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
Every dot is a real subway train. Eight hundred of them, give or take, form a small jazz combo (walking bass, piano, sax, vibes, brushes) that has been playing without pause for over a hundred years. On the platforms they are hot, screaming, full of complaint. This is the music inside the noise.  The harmony moves through a slow chorus. A note is placed precisely where the train happens to be along its route. Rush hour fills the band with held tones; at 3 a.m. the silences grow longer. Whatever is playing now has not played before and will not play again.  Share your location and the trains nearest you grow louder. The piece rearranges itself around your body. You are listening to a portrait of where you stand, played by the city you are standing in.
Joshua Wolk is a designer and engineer who leverages data to make art.
We'll explore:
* The music all around us in every day life.
* The science of sound design.
* Basic music theory as applied to locomotives.
This might be for you if you...

events.name: Histories Of Freedom, Justice, and Democracy
events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
 💭 Topic: "Freedom, Justice, and Democracy: History of the Reconstruction and Thaddeus Stevens" 🎤 Lecturer: Stephanie Townrow 📆 Date: Friday, September 9th ⏰ Doors Open: 6:30 PM 📍 Location: Dumbo, Brooklyn
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
🤝 A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
When the Civil War ended, the United States faced an enormous question: What kind of country would it become? Congressman Thaddeus Stevens believed the nation could not simply rebuild what had existed before the war. Instead, he called for radical changes to dismantle the South's old social and economic system, protect the rights of formerly enslaved people, and create a country built on a foundation of legal equality. This talk explores Stevens' bold vision for Reconstruction, the fierce opposition he faced, and why the questions he raised about freedom, justice, and democracy remain just as relevant today.

Stephanie Townrow is the Director of Interpretation and Exhibitions at the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center for History and Democracy, a new museum she has had the privilege to build from the ground-up. A Ph.D. candidate in American history at the University of Delaware, she specializes in bringing the past to life through storytelling, artifacts, and the occasional deep dive down a historical rabbit hole. She has spent the last several years immersed in the world of Thaddeus Stevens and Lydia Hamilton Smith—and promises that Stevens was far more interesting (and important) than most history textbooks let on. She's excited to share some of the surprising stories behind one of America's most fascinating and fearless politicians.
We'll explore:
* The reconstruction of the United States post Civil War
* The radical changes that occured during this period which have led to the state of the country we live in today
* The role that Thaddeus Stevens played in shaping our nation
This might be for you if you...
* Are curious about unknown figures in our shared history
* Are intrigued by the steps taken by the government during the Reconstruction era that have directly impacted where the US is today
* Enjoy lecture-based and conversation-focused events of any kind — think Ted Talks in bars, Lectures on Tap, or micro learning meets dinner party
* Want to switch up your usual weeknight. Why not make it interesting? 🤓

Build the full path from a stranger to a booked meeting to a closed deal, and know exactly what it costs you.

What’s covered

Build the complete sales funnel, not just the top of it.

You’ll learn how to attract and capture leads, qualify them so you spend time on the right prospects, automatically book meetings, follow up without losing anyone, and measure what every stage costs.

What you’ll do

Attract and capture

Map the entire funnel with Claude, stage by stage.
Create a lead magnet that solves one urgent problem.
Build a landing page and opt-in form that captures the lead.

Qualify

Add qualifying questions covering budget, timeline, need, and decision-making authority.
Use Claude and your CRM’s lead scoring to automatically separate hot leads from cold ones.

Book meetings

Connect a scheduling tool so qualified leads can instantly book a call.
Add confirmations and reminders designed to reduce no-shows.

Follow up and close

Write a nurture sequence and automated follow-ups with Claude.
Include dedicated paths for no-shows and rescheduling.
Configure your CRM to draft a personalized follow-up after each meeting so no opportunity quietly evaporates.

Measure the money

Set up the numbers that determine whether the funnel is working, including cost per lead, cost per booked meeting, customer acquisition cost, and conversion rates between each stage.
Use Claude to interpret the dashboard, identify where money is leaking, and suggest what to fix first.

The proposal also highlights two longer-term metrics founders should watch: lifetime value compared with customer acquisition cost, and the time required to recover acquisition costs.

Recommended stack: Claude for copy, scoring logic, and interpreting performance; HubSpot’s free CRM for lead capture, scoring, pipeline management, and reporting; Calendly or Cal.com for scheduling; and Systeme.io as an all-in-one option for landing pages, email, and funnels.

Other tools considered: Chili Piper and RevenueHero for high-volume inbound teams, ClickFunnels for templates, GoHighLevel for agencies, and ActiveCampaign for advanced email automation.

You’ll leave with: A live funnel that captures, qualifies, books, and follows up with leads, plus a simple dashboard showing what each stage costs.

Programming note: The proposal identifies this as the most content-dense session and suggests that it may work better as two separate evenings, one focused on building and capturing leads, and another focused on qualification, booking, and measurement.

events.name: Drop-In Men's Work Group
events.description:
A meeting where men can do their work.
Men’s work is just this: being mindful and relating intentionally with other people who identify as men, to allow ourselves to just be, together, in a deeper way. We sometimes call this deeper connection "dropping in".

Men’s work can help to expand emotional range and resilience, and your ability to express feelings - here in the group through creating a safe space, and out in the world, at your job and in your relationships.

This circle is for both men who have experienced men's work and for men who are curious about men's work.

Anyone who identifies as male can join.

How it will work

We'll meet from 6:30 PM sharp until 8:30PM. Please come sober, with your phone off, and ready to spend the whole time with the group.

Expect a series of conversations and guided experiences to connect you more deeply to yourself and to others.

Please Note: This is not therapy.
This is a mutual support group, hosted by peers.
About your Host, Daniel Stillman

I work as executive leadership coach and keynote speaker, for organizations of all shapes, sizes and industries. I have learned that at the heart of real change is a conversation - one with yourself, as well as conversations with others. I create space for leaders and their teams to have the conversations that matter.

I’ve been co-leading a men’s group since 2018, and have taught and facilitated men's work in person, online, and at multi-day retreats. Men’s work has been an important part of my ongoing personal development and has allowed me to expand my emotional range and resilience. It’s also expanded my range and the depth in my one-on-one coaching and team transformation work.

I also host The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management Podcast) and am the author of “Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter” a handbook for changemakers and innovators.

Learn more at www.DanielStillman.com

A portion of the proceeds from ticket sales will go to the Ever Forward Club, which provides support programs and workshops to disadvantaged young men and boys in the Bay Area.

Agreements for the gathering:

I agree to…

Come prepared and ready to both give and receive support for the group members by being well rested and nourished.  I will take care of myself.

I will include all the men in the conversation.  I will not dominate.

I will not be violent.

I agree to keep everything discussed or revealed in the group completely confidential except for what I share or another man’s reaction to what I share.  

I agree to keep the physical space we use and occupy in better shape than I found it.

For the duration of the session I will honor myself and my colleagues by not coming under the influence of any mood altering recreational substance, including drugs and alcohol. 

I agree that our time together is not counseling or therapy.  

If there is any reason to believe that I may be of harm to myself or others, I am required to share this with the group.

Stop the week from leaking. Build the system that runs everything that isn’t the product.

What’s covered

Create the operating system for a one-person company.

This session covers how to plan your work, use AI throughout the day, connect the tools you already rely on, automate repetitive tasks, and establish a rhythm that keeps the business moving.

What you’ll do

Map your operation

Identify where your time, attention, and money are leaking across your inbox, calendar, notes, follow-ups, and administrative work.

Build your hub

Set up one central workspace for your tasks, documents, projects, and roadmap.

Wire in Claude

Turn meeting notes into actionable tasks.

Automate the busywork

Examples might include sending a new lead into your CRM with a follow-up task, or transforming meeting notes into assigned action items.

Add guardrails and rhythm

events.name: UGLY TALK X GOOD TALK: WHAT NO ONE TELLS YOU ABOUT BEING A MIDDLE AGED FOUNDER
events.description:
A small, facilitated roundtable for founders who aren't hustle-culture kids.
Bring one conversation you've been avoiding. Leave with real perspective on it, and a handful of founders who know what you're actually dealing with.
No stage. No audience. No pitching. 
Facilitated by executive leadership coach Daniel Stillman, author of Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter. 
Who is this for?
Being a founder takes commitment, sacrifice, and sometimes hustle. But the hustle-culture narrative doesn't match the life you want as you get older. You're not 25 with nothing to lose. You have a mortgage. You want a proper vacation. Maybe you have aging parents to care for. And a mission you still want to bring into the world. 

Why a Roundtable?
You don’t need another big networking event, or a poorly moderated panel you could have watched on YouTube at 2x.

You need an intimate, high-trust, off-the-record room where you can get real with other founders, builders and entrepreneurs. 

A roundtable is one where everyone shares, everyone is heard, and everyone gets more than they imagined.

The Conversation
Conversations are the atomic unit of change. Our lives are built by the conversations we have, and defined by the ones we avoid. The cofounder conflict you brush off but never resolve. The hire you won't admit isn't working. The pivot you keep putting off.
The ones we avoid most are with ourselves. The bargains we never renegotiated. The anxiety we can't politely ask to leave. The question we keep not answering.
The un-had conversation doesn't disappear. It goes underground and gets more expensive. This roundtable is designed to create the space for the most important questions and conversations you’re facing right now.

Application and Curation
Admission is by invitation only - please complete all application questions so we can curate the group, optimizing for:

People actively building
Openness, Curiosity and Generosity
Commitment - people who don’t show up won’t be invited to come again
The Prework: 
This is a small room, on purpose, so we’re only selecting a handful of folks who are willing to do some thinking before they get in the room. Apply with your thoughtful answers to the registration questions.
The Format: 
Five rounds of conversation: 
Connection and Learning - so we know who we are and why we’re building what we are each building
Exploration: Sharing your avoided conversation with the group
Stories Vs Advice: Sharing stories to help each other through shared empathy, not problem solving
Asks and Offers: What’s something you need from the group? What’s something you can offer in generosity?
Closing Round - What you’re taking away from the conversation - what you’re committed to
The Follow Up:
Join a continuing conversation with the attendees, where you can share the resource you mentioned, ask that follow-up question, and get the support you need from a generous, growing community.
Your Co-Hosts
Daniel Stillman designs conversations for a living, and insists that you do too. He's an executive coach and facilitator who works with founders and founding teams on how they lead, communicate, and navigate the conversations that matter. He hosts The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management podcast) and wrote Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter, a handbook for changemakers and innovators.
Anson Wu is the founder of Ugly Talk, the no-BS event series where battle-tested founders share the setbacks, pivots, and lessons behind the wins. Since 2019 it's grown across New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami. Anson also runs Grey Journal, the digital media company behind it, and came up as a designer and agency founder. By his own description, a recovering underthinker still mining the lessons from two failed startups.
About Ugly Talk
Started in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough “aha!” moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons and insights.
With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami, we’ve built a vibrant community of thousands of founders and industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape.
Official Website: UglyTalk.com
